title: Developer Relations & Advocacy
description: Master developer relations, advocacy, technical content creation, developer experience (DX), community architecture, open source stewardship, and developer marketing.

phases.title: DevRel & Content Foundations
phases.focus: The DevRel Flywheel, Technical Writing, API DX & Community Architecture

phases.title: Advocacy & Community Stewardship
phases.focus: Sample Apps, Public Speaking, Open Source Community, Product Advocacy & Orbit Metrics

phases.title: Advanced Developer Programs
phases.focus: Video/Streaming, Ambassador Programs, SDK Ergonomics, Launches & DX Audits

phases.title: DevRel Strategy & Team Building
phases.focus: Executive DevRel Strategy, Proving ROI, and Scaling Advocacy Teams

nodes.title: Developer Relations Foundations & The Flywheel
nodes.subtitle: DevRel definition, Developer Experience (DX), product feedback loops, DevRel flywheel
learning_objectives: Explain the four pillars of DevRel: Documentation, Community, Advocacy, and Marketing
Map the developer adoption journey from awareness to champion
feynman_prompts: What makes developer relations fundamentally different from traditional marketing?
key_misconceptions: Treating DevRel as pure sales promotion rather than genuine developer advocacy

nodes.title: Technical Content & Developer Blogging
nodes.subtitle: Tutorial design, code snippet clarity, SEO for technical searches, thought leadership
learning_objectives: Write engaging, copy-paste-runnable tutorials solving specific developer problems
Optimize technical content for long-tail search queries without keyword stuffing
feynman_prompts: Why must every code snippet in a developer tutorial be tested and runnable?
key_misconceptions: Writing shallow high-level marketing articles that lack actual code implementation

nodes.title: API Design, SDKs & Developer Onboarding
nodes.subtitle: Time-to-hello-world (TTHW), OpenAPI specs, SDK ergonomics, friction logging
learning_objectives: Conduct friction logs on developer signup and API authentication workflows
Optimize developer onboarding to achieve under 5-minute Time-to-Hello-World
feynman_prompts: What is 'friction logging' and why is it essential for API products?
key_misconceptions: Assuming developers will read a 50-page manual before attempting to run an API call

nodes.title: Community Architecture (Discord, Discourse, Slack)
nodes.subtitle: Community onboarding, channel taxonomy, moderation guidelines, gamification vs engagement
learning_objectives: Architect a welcoming community server structure with clear channels and code of conduct
Implement moderation bots and community safety guidelines
feynman_prompts: Why is Discourse/forums often better than Discord/Slack for searchable technical questions?
key_misconceptions: Measuring community health purely by raw member count rather than active helpful engagement

nodes.title: Reference Architectures & Sample Applications
nodes.subtitle: Starter templates, demo apps, monorepos, GitHub template repos, stack diversity
learning_objectives: Build production-ready starter applications showcasing SDK best practices
Maintain sample repositories with automated CI test runs to prevent code rot
feynman_prompts: Why is a complete full-stack sample app better than disconnected code snippets?
key_misconceptions: Allowing sample application dependencies to become deprecated and broken over time

nodes.title: Technical Speaking & Live Coding Demos
nodes.subtitle: Conference talk proposals (CFPs), slide design, live demo safety nets, vocal delivery
learning_objectives: Draft compelling conference CFP submissions that get accepted
Execute live coding presentations with pre-recorded fallback videos for emergencies
feynman_prompts: What are the three essential backup plans every presenter needs for a live demo?
key_misconceptions: Reading code line-by-line off a dense slide rather than explaining concepts visually

nodes.title: Open Source Stewardship & GitHub Management
nodes.subtitle: CONTRIBUTING guides, issue triage, good-first-issues, pull request reviews, license compliance
learning_objectives: Curate welcoming good-first-issues to attract first-time open source contributors
Review community PRs with constructive, appreciative feedback
feynman_prompts: Why is transparent public triage on GitHub essential for developer trust?
key_misconceptions: Leaving community issues and pull requests unanswered for weeks without acknowledgment

nodes.title: Hackathon Organization & Event Mentorship
nodes.subtitle: Judging criteria, API bounties, mentoring hackers, logistics, sponsorship activations
learning_objectives: Design engaging hackathon challenge prompts and fair scoring rubrics
Provide hands-on architectural troubleshooting support to hackathon teams under deadlines
feynman_prompts: What makes a hackathon workshop effective for developers under time pressure?
key_misconceptions: Delivering a 60-minute theoretical pitch at a hackathon instead of a 15-minute quickstart demo

nodes.title: Internal Advocacy: Bridging Users to Product
nodes.subtitle: Aggregating community feedback, bug advocacy, PM alignment, customer sentiment reports
learning_objectives: Synthesize scattered Discord/GitHub feedback into actionable product bug tickets
Represent developer pain points in internal sprint planning meetings
feynman_prompts: How does a developer advocate defend user interests without alienating internal engineering?
key_misconceptions: Acting as an uncritical megaphone for user complaints rather than curating actionable data

nodes.title: DevRel Metrics & The Orbit Model
nodes.subtitle: Orbit model (Love, Reach, Gravity), qualified developer leads, attribution, NPS
learning_objectives: Track community growth and member progression using the Orbit framework
Demonstrate DevRel business impact without reducing developers to sales funnels
feynman_prompts: Why does the traditional sales funnel fail to capture developer advocacy and community gravity?
key_misconceptions: Attributing individual customer enterprise contracts directly to a single conference talk

nodes.title: Video Content, Live Streaming & Workshops
nodes.subtitle: YouTube tutorials, Twitch live coding, podcasting, production equipment, editing
learning_objectives: Produce high-retention technical YouTube walkthroughs with chapters and visual overlays
Host interactive live coding streams handling real-time viewer questions
feynman_prompts: How does audience pacing differ in a recorded tutorial versus a live interactive stream?
key_misconceptions: Producing low-energy, rambling 2-hour streams with zero structure or prepared milestones

nodes.title: Champions & Ambassador Programs
nodes.subtitle: Developer MVP programs, swag distribution, early access betas, community councils
learning_objectives: Design an exclusive developer champions program that rewards top community contributors
Organize private feedback sessions and roadmap previews for trusted ambassadors
feynman_prompts: What motivates top developers to contribute to an ambassador program beyond free swag?
key_misconceptions: Exploiting community champions for free labor without providing genuine career visibility

nodes.title: SDK Ergonomics & Language Idioms
nodes.subtitle: Type safety, error handling idioms across languages (Pythonic, Go, JS), async client patterns
learning_objectives: Design client libraries that feel native to each specific programming language ecosystem
Implement resilient retry policies and clear error hierarchies across SDKs
feynman_prompts: Why does generating an SDK strictly via OpenAPI generator often result in poor DX?
key_misconceptions: Directly porting Java-style object conventions into a Python or Go SDK

nodes.title: Developer Marketing, Show HN & Launch Strategy
nodes.subtitle: Hacker News etiquette, Product Hunt launches, Reddit r/programming, technical PR
learning_objectives: Draft genuine 'Show HN' posts that resonate with technical audiences and adhere to rules
Orchestrate multi-channel product launches across developer communities
feynman_prompts: Why will aggressive marketing speak instantly cause a developer launch to fail on Hacker News?
key_misconceptions: Using marketing buzzwords (revolutionary, disruptive) when describing a technical API

nodes.title: Global DevRel & Localized Communities
nodes.subtitle: Regional developer ecosystems (LATAM, EMEA, APAC), translation, cultural etiquette
learning_objectives: Adapt DevRel strategy to distinct international developer ecosystems and developer hubs
Support community-led translation and regional meetup chapters
feynman_prompts: How do developer adoption patterns and payment models vary across global regions?
key_misconceptions: Assuming developer tool adoption patterns in San Francisco reflect developer workflows worldwide

nodes.title: Developer Experience (DX) Auditing
nodes.subtitle: End-to-end friction audits, cognitive load scoring, error message UX, documentation audits
learning_objectives: Execute deep developer experience audits for third-party tools and internal platforms
Score cognitive load and compile prioritized DX remediation roadmaps
feynman_prompts: What makes error documentation in an API as important as the primary endpoint documentation?
key_misconceptions: Auditing DX only on the happy path while ignoring rate limit errors and invalid tokens

nodes.title: DevRel Strategy & Executive Alignment
nodes.subtitle: DevRel business case, budgeting, proving ROI to the CFO, organizational placement
learning_objectives: Align DevRel team goals directly with company revenue, hiring, and product adoption
Secure long-term DevRel budgets during macroeconomic downturns
feynman_prompts: How do you defend the value of developer relations when the CFO asks for immediate ROI?
key_misconceptions: Positioning DevRel as an unaccountable travel-and-t-shirt hobby team

nodes.title: Building, Leading & Scaling DevRel Teams
nodes.subtitle: DevRel team archetypes, hiring technical advocates, preventing advocate burnout
learning_objectives: Structure DevRel teams balancing community, documentation, and evangelism specializations
Manage continuous conference travel schedules to prevent advocate burnout
feynman_prompts: Why is travel burnout the primary reason senior developer advocates leave the profession?
key_misconceptions: Expecting a single developer advocate to be a world-class coder, speaker, writer, and event planner
